subject: general-mathematics
title: Arithmetic progressions
summary: Sequences that go up or down by the same amount: the nth term and the sum.

lesson.text: An arithmetic progression (AP) is a sequence where you add the same number each time. In 3, 7, 11, 15, ... you add 4 each time.

items: Common difference: d = any term minus the one before (here d = 7 − 3 = 4). d can be negative.

lesson.text: T_n = a + (n − 1)d. To reach the nth term, you add d one less time than n.

lesson.title: The 1st term is 5 and the 6th term is 30. Find d.

lesson.text: The sum of the first n terms
S_n = n/2 × [2a + (n − 1)d], or S_n = n/2 × (first term + last term).

lesson.title: Saving: ₦1,000 in week 1, ₦1,500 in week 2, ₦2,000 in week 3, ...

lesson.text: The most common slip is using n instead of (n − 1). The 1st term has no d added at all.

questions.explanation: d = 17 − 20 = −3. The sequence goes down, so d is negative.

Which of these is an arithmetic progression?
questions.explanation: 2, 5, 8, 11 adds 3 each time. 2, 4, 8, 16 and 3, 6, 12, 24 double (geometric); 1, 4, 9, 16 are squares.
